answer: According to Section 126(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, wrongful restraint occurs when a person voluntarily obstructs another person, preventing them from proceeding in any direction they have the right to proceed. This act is punishable under Section 126(2) with simple imprisonment for up to one month, a fine of up to five thousand rupees, or both.
summary_answer: Wrongful restraint is the act of voluntarily obstructing a person from proceeding in any direction they have the right to go.
detailed_answer: According to Section 126(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, wrongful restraint occurs when a person voluntarily obstructs another person, preventing them from proceeding in any direction they have the right to proceed. This act is punishable under Section 126(2) with simple imprisonment for up to one month, a fine of up to five thousand rupees, or both.
final_answer: Wrongful restraint is defined as the voluntary obstruction of a person, preventing them from proceeding in any direction they have the right to go, punishable under Section 126 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.
